quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What do no passing zone signs and lane markings tell you?

options.text: There are oncoming cars passing in your direction.
You can only pass during daylight hours.
You cannot see far enough ahead to pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see far enough ahead to pass safely.
questions.explanation: No passing zones mean you cannot see far enough ahead to pass safely. It is dangerous to pass where another vehicle might enter or cross the road. These areas include intersections, railroad crossings, and shopping center entrances.

questions.question: You are driving at the speed limit when the traffic light turns yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and go through the intersection without caution.
Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Stop before entering the intersection, if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming soon. Stop at a yellow light if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, cross the intersection carefully.

questions.question: If your car is about to be hit from behind, you should NOT:

options.text: Release your seat belt.
Brace yourself.
Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release your seat belt.
questions.explanation: If your car is hit from behind, your body will be thrown backward. Brace yourself by pressing against the back of your seat and placing your head against the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Hold the steering wheel firmly and be ready to brake.

questions.question: What does this speed limit sign mean?

options.text: You must drive through the intersection at exactly 55 mph.
The maximum speed is 55 mph under ideal conditions.
You cannot drive slower than 55 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum speed is 55 mph under ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the highest legal speed for this road. You can drive slower based on conditions, but you cannot drive faster than the posted limit.

questions.question: Which factor affects how fast your body absorbs alcohol?

options.text: Weight
Height
Intelligence

questions.correctAnswerText: Weight
questions.explanation: Your weight, biological sex, how much food you have eaten, and how many drinks you have had all affect alcohol absorption. The only way to remove alcohol from your body is to wait.

questions.question: Why is nighttime driving more dangerous than daytime driving?

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead at night.
The road is always more slippery at night.
Your reaction time is slower at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead at night.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead because of darkness and the glare from oncoming headlights. Always use your headlights and drive carefully at night.

questions.question: A vehicle heading toward you has its high beams on and is blinding you. What should you do?

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at the oncoming headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the other car from the corner of your eye.

questions.question: What should you do before entering a curve?

options.text: Turn on your turn signal.
Reduce your speed.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: You must slow down for curves where you cannot see far ahead. Other situations requiring slower speed include hills with limited visibility, slippery roads, and areas with pedestrians or animals.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is approaching with its flashing lights on. What must you do?

options.text: Stay in your lane and keep your speed until it passes.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Pull to the edge of the road and stop until it passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the edge of the road and stop until it passes.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, pull to the right edge of the road and stop. Stay parallel to the curb. On one-way streets, move to whichever edge is closest to you.

questions.question: After a train passes the railroad crossing, what should you do before crossing?

options.text: Wait for the signal lights to stop flashing.
Look for a second train.
Do both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do both of the above.
questions.explanation: After a train passes, watch for a second train on any track. Do not cross until all gates are raised and all warning lights have stopped flashing.

questions.question: What does a yellow left arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: You should get ready to yield to oncoming traffic.
The protected left turn is ending soon.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: A yellow left arrow means the protected left turn is ending. You must get ready to yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is correct?

options.text: You can eliminate blind spots by having one outside mirror on each side of your vehicle.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can see all blind spots by looking in your rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have larger blind spots, so stay away from them.

questions.question: When you merge onto a freeway, you should drive:

options.text: At the same speed as the traffic on the freeway.
Five to 10 mph slower than freeway traffic.
At the posted speed limit for the freeway.

questions.correctAnswerText: At the same speed as the traffic on the freeway.
questions.explanation: When merging onto a freeway, match the speed of traffic on the freeway.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down or stop.
Stop if necessary.
You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line. Stop before a crosswalk if there is no stop line. If there is no crosswalk, stop at a point where you can see oncoming traffic.

questions.question: As you drive faster, what is important to do?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Look far ahead of your vehicle.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: As you drive faster, your vehicle needs more distance to stop. Look far ahead so you have time to react safely to hazards.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should check your mirrors and:

options.text: Never look over your right shoulder.
Always slow down in your lane.
Look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder. Make sure no vehicle is in the lane you want to enter and that no one is trying to enter from another direction.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines down the center of a road mean about passing?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from your direction.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double yellow lines mean no one can cross the center line to pass, no matter which direction you are traveling.

questions.question: How can you avoid skidding on slippery surfaces?

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.
Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve. Braking in a curve can cause you to skid.

questions.question: What does a red arrow pointing right on a traffic light mean?

options.text: You may turn right after slowing down and checking traffic.
You cannot turn right until the light turns green.
You may turn right after coming to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn right until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. You must wait until a green light or green arrow appears. Do not turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?

options.text: In an intersection where there are no oncoming vehicles
Wherever signs and road markings allow passing
In a curve where there are no oncoming vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever signs and road markings allow passing
questions.explanation: Never pass in intersections, parking lot entrances, or alleyways. Never pass on curves or hills where you cannot see oncoming traffic. Only pass where signs and road markings permit it and when you have enough space to do so safely.

questions.question: You are 16 or 17 years old. You are convicted of driving more than 20 miles per hour over the speed limit. How long will your license be suspended?

options.text: 30 days.
45 days.
60 days.

questions.correctAnswerText: 60 days.
questions.explanation: If you are 16 or 17 years old and convicted of speeding 20 mph over the limit for the first time, your license will be suspended for 60 days. You must also pay a restoration fee and court fines. The penalties are worse for repeat offenses.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lane markings mean?

options.text: Neither lane may pass.
Both lanes may pass.
The lane to the right may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Neither lane may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lane markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid yellow lines mean no one can pass in either direction.

questions.question: A traffic signal is not working. What should you do?

options.text: Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.
If the intersection is clear, you do not need to stop.
Drive quickly through the intersection to get out of the way of other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: When a traffic signal is not working, treat the intersection as an all-way stop. Come to a complete stop unless a police officer is directing traffic. Look and yield before entering the intersection.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Jogging trail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign shows a pedestrian crosswalk. When you see it, be alert and let pedestrians cross safely.

questions.question: When are collisions most likely to happen?

options.text: All vehicles are traveling at about the same speed.
One lane of traffic is traveling faster than the other lanes.
One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Collisions happen more often when one vehicle travels faster or slower than the other vehicles around it. Speeding increases crash risk. Driving too slowly is also dangerous because it can cause rear-end collisions or make other drivers swerve to avoid you.
